what: Whisper through the davidmiheev/candle fork: first candle-examples/examples/whisper (2026-09-20), then ignite-catalog's candle-transcription executor itself (2026-09-24, see executor_run).
hardware: Kaggle Tesla T4, sm_75, CUDA 12.8, torch 2.10.0+cu128
headline: The fork's whisper EXAMPLE returns an empty transcription for every one of 40 isolated spoken digits, while the transformers implementation of the same weights reads them at 0.75 exact-match. The same binary transcribes the example's own long samples correctly, so this is a property of that example's decode on short utterances and not of the build or of the harness around it.

measured.candle_output_shape: loads pcm, builds mel [1, 80, 3000], reports one segment, emits no text
measured.unpadded_control: identical -- empty with and without 0.5 s of leading/trailing silence

positive_control.sample:jfk: 1.8s-10.4s:  and so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you ask what you can do for your country
positive_control.sample:gb1: 30.0s -- 60.0s 1.8s-4.4s:  and the Lord was a crew of seven. Colonel Rick Husband, Lieutenant Colonel Michael Anderson,

resampler_question: The ignite-catalog transcription executor resamples 8 kHz to 16 kHz with plain linear interpolation and no anti-aliasing filter. Run against scipy's polyphase resampler on the same clips and the same engines, the two give IDENTICAL scores: 0.75 for transformers either way. On this corpus the crude resampler costs nothing.
lead_not_verified: CORRECTED 2026-09-25. An earlier version said the fork carries a rewritten apply_timestamp_rules that upstream does not have. That is wrong: candle-examples/examples/whisper/main.rs is byte-identical between davidmiheev/candle main (upstream 0.11.0) and ignite-perf, and apply_timestamp_rules came from upstream huggingface/candle#3054. What the record does show: the example ran with timestamps on and, for every digit, printed one timestamped span with no text (e.g. '0.0s-1.8s: '), so the window was decoded and kept -- not dropped by the example's no-speech skip (no_speech_prob > 0.6 and avg_logprob < -1), whose 'no speech detected' message appears only for the trailing silent window of gb1. A decoder that closes its first timestamp pair immediately would produce exactly this on short utterances while leaving long ones intact. Still NOT verified; it is where to look, and it is upstream's code.

fixes_required: candle-transformers does not build without CUDA: candle_nn::fused::static_decode is #[cfg(feature = "cuda")] but called from ungated sites. 52 errors with --features mkl. This contradicts ignite-catalog's whisper-cpu.yaml, which declares gpu.required: false. The fork's ignite-perf has since added a CPU stub for static_decode that returns an error at call time.

candle-examples declares symphonia 0.6.0 (which resolves to 0.6.1; the fork gitignores Cargo.lock, so nothing pins it) while its audio code uses the 0.5 API -- AudioBufferRef, codecs::DecoderOptions, core::conv, core::probe. 6 errors, breaking every symphonia example: whisper, encodec, mimi, snac. The 0.6.0 declaration is upstream's (huggingface/candle#3546), not the fork's. Pinned to 0.5.4 to build; the fork's ignite-perf now carries that pin.
the whisper target additionally requires --features symphonia alongside cuda
CUDA 12.8 needs the compatibility.cuh __hmax_nan guard extended with CURART_VERSION < 12000
the Kaggle image ships no Rust and no libcuda.so on the usual paths; the driver is at /usr/local/nvidia/lib64

my_own_errors_on_the_way: scored a numeral transcription ('1.', '3') as an empty string by stripping non-alphabetic characters, which understated transformers from 0.75 to 0.25 -- the same bug was in rung I2
piped cargo into tail, so the build reported tail's exit status (the BUILD_EXIT=0 trap)
passed --timestamps false to a clap flag that takes no value
published the candle checkout into /kaggle/working, making the output undownloadable

scope_correction.what_was_run: candle-examples/examples/whisper built from davidmiheev/candle@ignite-perf (upstream code: the fork does not change this example)
scope_correction.why_it_matters: They share the model (candle_transformers::models::whisper) and nothing else that decides this result. The executor carries its own Decoder (lib.rs:389) with zero references to apply_timestamp_rules -- the upstream function this record names as the lead -- decodes each window at a single temperature with no fallback loop, and resolves a no_timestamps_token. So the empty-transcription finding most likely does NOT transfer to the executor, and an earlier version of this record said 'the fork's whisper' in a way that implied it did.
scope_correction.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-24: the executor itself has now been run -- see executor_run. It does not return empty transcriptions.

executor_run.what: models/executors/exp/candle-transcription (ignite-catalog@perf/exp-executors) run as the executor runs, one request per file through its own transcribe_blocking: symphonia decode, its linear resampler, candle's pcm_to_mel, its own Decoder. Only the ignite SDK plumbing was removed (request parsing, the async wrappers, and ignite_asset::AssetLoader, replaced by a local directory holding the same four file names). The harness source is not committed here because the catalog is private.
executor_run.hardware: Kaggle Tesla T4 (sm_75), CUDA 12.8; build 549 s with --features cuda against davidmiheev/candle@9aa02f1
executor_run.clips: 61 requests per arm: 50 isolated digits from part I's held-out speaker (the raw 8 kHz files), ten 4-digit sequences, and samples_jfk.wav
executor_run.headline: The executor never returns an empty transcription (0 of 427 requests across 7 arms), so the example's empty-output bug does not reach the production decode path. Static decode and the CUDA graph produce byte-identical text to eager decoding on every request, as does CPU. It has four real defects of its own: nonsense language reports on English-only models, a task token English-only models were never trained with, token suppression silently skipped for the model the catalog registers, and an asset named for 80 mel filters that panics if it holds 80.

scores.note: digit exact = the digit read correctly (numerals and homophones normalised); seq WER over ten 4-digit clips; JFK WER; median seconds per request INCLUDING model load, as the executor loads per request

agreement.turbo language auto vs forced en: 48/61 identical -- omitting the language token changes 13 transcripts ('Oui.' vs 'We.', '3.' vs 'three.')
agreement.candle tiny.en vs transformers, the exec: 46/61 -- matching the prompt explains about half the disagreement

defects.evidence: detect_language argmaxes over every <|xx|> token in the vocab; tiny.en has those tokens but was never trained on them. It reports 'sq' (Albanian) for JFK and ms/km/hi/ca for the digits, and the reported language changes between eager, static and CPU runs of identical text. Report-only (not injected), so the text is unaffected, but the response's language field is wrong for every .en model.
defects.fix: skip detection (report 'en') when the checkpoint is English-only

defects.what: <|transcribe|> in the prompt of English-only models
defects.evidence: the executor always decodes from [SOT, (lang), transcribe, notimestamps]; English-only Whisper was trained from [SOT, notimestamps]. Measured in transformers with the same greedy loop on the same bytes: tiny.en digit exact 0.48 -> 0.64, sequence WER 0.10 -> 0.175. It is a different model behaviour, not a uniformly worse one.
defects.fix: omit the task token when the vocab has no multilingual prompt, as transformers does

defects.evidence: the candle Config reads suppress_tokens from config.json; whisper-large-v3-turbo keeps them in generation_config.json, so its config.json list is empty and the executor applies no suppression to the model the catalog registers. transformers applies them.

the executor loads 'melfilters80.bytes'; large-v3-turbo needs 128 mel bins. With a genuine 80-filter file the request panics: index out of bounds in candle-transformers/src/models/whisper/audio.rs:153 (len 16080, index 16080). So production either stores 128 filters under the name '80', or crashes. Which one is not observable from here.
defects.fix: name the asset by the checkpoint's num_mel_bins, and check its length against n_mel * (n_fft/2+1) before use

defects.what: auto language detection costs a second encoder pass
defects.evidence: detect_language runs the encoder on the first window, then decode runs it again: 2.83 s median per request with auto against 1.94 s with language=en (turbo, T4).

executor_run.not_isolated: With prompts matched, candle and transformers still disagree on 15/61 tiny.en and ~21-24/61 turbo transcripts, including hallucinations only on the candle side ('Thank you for watching.', 'for the next couple of months.' for a single spoken digit). Candidates are the mel front end (candle's own FFT, padding and melfilters.bytes against transformers' feature extractor) and f32 vs fp16. Not tested.
executor_run.also: the executor Cargo manifest uses the fork's static_decode path and candle_core::cuda_backend::graph ungated, so like candle-transformers it does not build without --features cuda -- the same contradiction with whisper-cpu.yaml's gpu.required: false.
